title: The 300-HP Lexus Q-Ship Hiding A Bulletproof V8 Under Anonymous Sheetmetal - HotCars
content: By the late 1990s, Japanese brands had mastered the art of creating cars that were more than met the eye. Their European competitors were going big and bold, setting out their stall for what type of audience this car was going for. But Japanese luxury was more understated, quiet, and subtle. Sophisticated engineering, powerful engines, and surprising capability could all be hidden underneath more ordinary styling, creating a contrast between performance and appearance. But for those who knew, there was an exciting car underneath. By the late 1990s, Japanese automakers had spent years proving that they could match European manufacturers’ quality and technology. European brands like     Mercedes-Benz and BMW had built sportier models with reputations for aggressive styling and impressive performance — cars like the BMW E46 M3, E39 M5, or Mercedes-Benz E55 AMG — while Lexus instead focused more on subtlety, restraint, and a more anonymous aesthetic. This philosophy was very evident in the luxury sedan market. Where BMW and Mercedes-Benz's offerings would attract attention wherever they went, Lexus more commonly flew under the radar despite packing sophisticated engineering and, increasingly, powerful V8s under their hoods. It was a stark difference to their European counterparts, and helped to create something exciting: sleepers. Quiet confidence is what a sleeper is all about. It's knowing that you have far more power and capability than you let on, safe in the knowledge that you could deploy it whenever you wanted. And while European brands favored stylistic choices that announced their power, Lexus was comfortable obscuring theirs under unassuming bodywork and conservative exterior choices. In doing so, they created something far more interesting. For some, there’s always been something compelling about a car that hides its true potential. Something that doesn’t look as fast as it truly is. And during the late 1990s/early 2000s, cars were definitely trying to look every bit as quick as they were. Big wings, flared arches, and loud exhausts were the order of the day. But sleepers deliberately went in the opposite direction, blending into traffic and letting their performance do the talking. This was also a perfect option for executive, luxury sedans. Their restrained styling and business-like demeanor meant that a driver could have both comfort and power, should they want it, while the untrained eye would look over the car with no indication of what it was capable of. And while some brands opted for this method, it was Lexus that was arguably the best at it. The Japanese brand’s cars were never the showiest, nor the loudest, but the V8 engines they concealed gave them an intriguing personality. They were more than happy to provide refinement and elegance when required, while also quietly providing straight-line speed that would make many performance cars blush. And there was one car that did this with devastating efficiency. The first-generation GS, which was Lexus’ answer to the European executive sedan and was known as the Toyota Aristo in Japan, arrived in the early 1990s. Designed by Italdesign Giugiaro, it was a good if not particularly sporty alternative. The second generation refined the formula, improving on the chassis and bringing in the 430 nameplate, though the car remained somewhat easy to overlook in a crowded marketplace. But by the third generation, the car had come into its own. It started with the chassis. The S190 chassis used in the third-gen GS 430 was more rigid than its predecessor, had a more sophisticated suspension setup (using double-wishbones rather than the MacPherson struts), and allowed for a greater rear-wheel-drive balance. But the chassis was only part of the equation, and another crucial improvement came in the car’s engine. The 4.3-liter 3UZ-FE V8 provided 300 horsepower and 325 lb-ft of torque at a time when competing cars like the E39 BMW 540i made around 282 hp and 325 lb-ft. Power was, naturally, sent exclusively to the rear wheels, which gave it a decidedly more sporting edge than one might have expected. The car wasn't exactly a lightweight, coming in at over 3,700 pounds, but it could still hit 60 mph in 6.0 seconds en route to an electronically limited 155 mph. And it did all this while wearing the sheet metal of a sensible banker, rather than a dominating performance vehicle. The car’s aesthetic was one of what Lexus called “L-finesse”, or “Leading-Edge Finesse”. A corporate design philosophy, it aimed to turn Lexus cars from their traditionally understated designs into something far bolder and more modern. It prioritized simplicity, elegance, and a driver-first approach that tried to place controls in positions that were instinctive to the driver. The third-generation GS 430 was the first production car to employ this new take, with elements like the sloping roofline and stance aimed squarely at its European contemporaries. The wood veneer and touchscreens on the interior offered improved ergonomics to the driver, too, placing them at the center of the driving experience. It made for the     ultimate sleeper. People looking in their rearview mirror and seeing a GS 430 might presume that it wouldn't be able to keep up, but would soon be surprised as the unassuming sedan not only blasted past, but did so with its driver seated in luxurious comfort. But while the interior was good, it was the engine that was the real star of the show. Being a subsidiary of Toyota, the Lexus engineers didn’t need to reinvent the wheel when it came to powering the third-gen GS 430. They simply took one of the most proven engines in Toyota's arsenal — the 3UZ-FE — and deployed it with devastating efficiency. A naturally-aspirated V8, it came from the already-popular UZ lineup and had been popular in the LS 430. Its aluminum block helped to keep weight down, while dual overhead cams and Variable Valve Timing with Intelligence (VVT-i) allowed it to benefit from Toyota’s hard-earned reputation for reliability. Being NA also meant that power delivery was immediate and predictable, as there was no waiting for turbos to spool or superchargers to work after asking the throttle for more. This was important, because the car wasn’t designed to be a stripped-back performance machine: it was supposed to be ready to both cruise effortlessly between meetings and then eat up back roads, depending on what the day called for. That dual-purpose character was what the car was made for, and which made it the executive sedan sleeper icon it is today. The GS 430 never gained the mainstream success of cars like the BMW 5 Series or the Mercedes-Benz E-Class. And that’s arguably part of its charm. It’s a hidden gem among car enthusiasts, a V-8-powered monster without the additional drama. The car also laid the foundations for the continuation of Lexus’ V-8 GS lineage, and the L-Finesse philosophy. The GS 460 would iterate on what the GS 430 started, taking power up to 342 hp and adding an eight-speed automatic transmission compared to the GS 430's six. But the GS 430 was the one that started it. Today, the car remains an affordable, reliable, discreet option for those who know what they’re looking at. It’s not going to generate the most attention, but it’s not supposed to. It does the job, and it does it very well. We want to hear from you. title: Justin Jefferson Lands at No. 19 on NFL’s Top 100 - Minnesota Vikings
content:
EAGAN, Minn. – Justin Jefferson is now 6-for-6 in the "NFL Top 100" list. Minnesota's all-star receiver landed at No. 19 in this year's rankings. Jefferson's sixth NFL season marked his sixth straight with 1,000 receiving yards. He finished the campaign with 84 catches for 1,048 yards and two touchdowns. Though his stats dipped a bit in a season he caught passes from three different quarterbacks, "Jets" helped the Vikings finish a roller-coaster season 5-0. Jefferson is entering his seventh season with 579 career receptions for 8,480 yards and 42 touchdowns. He received three straight Pro Bowl nods from 2020-22 and another following his 2024 performance highlighted by 1,533 yards and 10 touchdowns. Jefferson received First-Team All-Pro honors by The Associated Press following his 1,809-yards in 2022 and again after 2024. View photos of Vikings WR Justin Jefferson during the 2025 season. He was named the 2022 NFL Offensive Player of the Year after leading the league in catches and receiving yards. On Dec. 25, he broke Hall of Famer Randy Moss' NFL record for career receiving yards through six seasons. Jefferson enters his seventh pro season just nine receptions away from passing Randy Moss for second in team history. Launched in 2011, "NFL Top 100" is an ordering of the league's top players by their peers. Jefferson previously landed at No. 53 in 2021, No. 17 in 2022, No. 2 in 2023, No. 18 in 2024 and No. 10 last year. title: New Midsize GS Spied: Is BMW Resurrecting The F650GS Dakar? - ADV Pulse
content: BMW Motorrad is working on a new midsize GS, recently spotted in prototype form. The move follows the launch of the F 450 GS at EICMA 2025, which replaced the G 310 GS and marked a fresh start for BMW’s entry‑level adventure lineup. Reports from Europe indicate BMW is benchmarking the new bike against Honda’s Transalp and Yamaha’s Ténéré 700, using both as development yardsticks. At the same time, BMW’s partner TVS — which builds the F 450 GS in India — already supplies a revised version of the parallel twin to Norton for its Atlas models. That engine comes in at 585 cc and produces 70 horsepower. The prototype GS seems to borrow some of that engine’s DNA, yet the Atlas has differences that raise questions about how BMW will configure the motor. One of the most notable distinctions lies in the crankshaft design. Norton’s twin uses the class‑standard 270‑degree firing order, while the F 450 GS runs with an unconventional 135‑degree crankpin offset. Whether BMW will carry that unusual setup into the midsize GS remains to be seen. As for output, expectations point to somewhere around 70 hp, keeping it below the F 900 GS’s 105 hp but right in the mix with other midsize adventure machines. Weight will likely slot in between the F 450 GS and F 900 GS at around 450 pounds wet. The chassis points to a steel bridge frame that looks closer to the F 900 GS than the entry‑level sibling, with braking components borrowed from larger models. Tubeless cross-spoke wheel sizes — 21 inches up front and 18 inches at the rear — reinforce its off‑road intent. Ample ground clearance also points to a longer-travel suspension in the 9-inch range. The bodywork still shows signs of early development, yet some design cues are already taking shape. The headlight appears inspired by the R1300 GS, though the trademark GS beak has not yet been added. The overall proportions and profile are reminiscent of the Yamaha Tenere 700, which is the model BMW is clearly aiming its sights at. Naming also remains unknown. “F 600 GS” would fit neatly into BMW’s current scheme, while reviving the “F 650 GS” badge is another possibility. For many riders, the idea of a modern take on the old F 650 GS Dakar from the early 2000s would add an extra layer of intrigue, which could be a way BMW might connect past heritage with its future midsize offering. And as history has shown, actual displacement may not be the deciding factor — past GS models like the F 800 and F 900 GS share the same displacement (895cc) despite their different names. It’s also possible BMW will remove the current F 800 GS from the lineup once this model is launched. What’s clear is that BMW still has plenty of work ahead. A production‑ready midsize GS isn’t expected before 2028, but the prototype signals BMW’s intent to strengthen its hand in one of the most competitive segments of the adventure market. title: Navy F-4 pilot recalls being paralyzed after high Gs pinched neck nerve in mock dogfight Vs A-4s - The Aviation Geek Club
content: G-induced Loss Of Consciousness (G-LOC) incidents have caused fatal accidents in high performance aircraft capable of sustaining high g for extended periods. High-G training for pilots of high-performance aircraft or spacecraft often includes ground training for G-LOC in special centrifuges, with some profiles exposing pilots to 9 Gs for a sustained period. Nevertheless, only a few fighter pilots have experienced G-LOC incidents. Most of them have “greyed out” (loss of all color vision), less have blacked out (you can see nothing but are still conscious and can hear and function, all be it blind). If you G-LOC you are grounded and subjected to a physical exam, a few centrifuge rides and a dual flight before you go out single seat. John Chesire, former US Navy F-4 Phantom II pilot, recalls on Quora; ‘I once was involved with some air combat training off the California coast with multiple adversary aircraft from TOPGUN, Navy Fighter Weapons School and VF-126 A-4s. [It was the “many vs. only us four aircraft,” the ‘furball finale’ for the TG NFWS course. It was our last, graduation flight at the school.] ‘I was flying an F-4 Phantom when twisting my head back under a very high G-load, I apparently pinched a nerve in my neck that briefly stunned and paralyzed me. ‘It happened in a very high-G, nose-low turn. Although I was somewhat conscious, being stunned I was not in control of the aircraft. My hands were off the stick and I was limp but in pain. We were very near supersonic in a rather steep dive, and I did not have control. ‘My RIO in the back seat was screaming at me, asking frantically if I was OK! After a few seconds I regained my composure, gained control of the aircraft and told him I was, “OK” … except for the remaining sharp pain in my neck. ‘He said later if I had not immediately answered, he would have initiated automatic ejections for both of us. While that may have saved my life if I did not regain control, doing so at such a high-speed ejection would have injured us both significantly.’ ‘All’s well that ends well. My RIO and I still talk about that day long ago, and remember it vividly.’ What are you waiting for? Set your Throttles to Full AB and Join The Aviation Geek Club!

title: Karol G 'marriage proposal': Her reaction made the moment even better - HOLA
content: Karol G has been collecting unforgettable fan moments on her latest tour, but a 56-year-old concertgoer may have just delivered one of the boldest yet. During the Colombian superstar's third Los Angeles concert at SoFi Stadium on Sunday, Aug. 16, a fan decided that seeing Karol G perform wasn't enough. He apparently came prepared to shoot his shot with a marriage proposal. The playful exchange was captured on video and shared across social media, including an Instagram Reel describing the concertgoer as a 56-year-old fan who proposed marriage to the singer. Other posts circulating the clip identified him as a "56-year-old Gringo fan" who described himself as "single and available."  And Karol G's reaction made the moment even better. The surprise proposal happened during the final night of Karol G's three-concert run at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. SoFi Stadium's official schedule confirms that Karol G was booked for three consecutive shows on Aug. 14, 15 and 16 as part of her Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour, with the Aug. 16 performance beginning at 7 p.m. It was during that third show that the 56-year-old fan caught Karol G's attention. In clips circulating on Instagram, the concertgoer is identified as being 56 and "single and available," turning his interaction with the singer into what amounted to a very public dating application. The original Reel shared by entertainment account Desde La Curva describes the encounter as Karol G receiving a "propuesta de matrimonio," or marriage proposal, from the 56-year-old fan. Other accounts quickly picked up the moment, with one post declaring: "Un fan de 56 años le pidió matrimonio a Karol G en pleno show," meaning, "A 56-year-old fan asked Karol G to marry him in the middle of the show." This was not exactly a private candlelit proposal. Thousands of people were watching. Rather than brushing off the unexpected proposition, Karol G appeared amused by the exchange. The viral posts surrounding the moment emphasize the fan's declaration that he was "single and available," while footage and reposts show the singer engaging with him from the stage. Earlier this year, the 35-year-old singer discussed her relationship status and her thoughts on marriage and children following reports that she and Feid had ended their relationship. Karol G has also previously revealed that when it comes to an actual marriage proposal, the moment matters more to her than the ring. During a dating-themed interview, she was asked what she would do if a boyfriend proposed with a ring she hated. "I don't care," Karol G responded, explaining, "I care more about the moment when he asked me." As for her ideal proposal? "A really unique one," she said as reported by DailyMotion. "Be creative." Well, proposing from the audience of a packed SoFi Stadium certainly checks the "unique" box. Whether it checks any of the others is another question. The proposal is the latest in a growing collection of unpredictable interactions between Karol G and her fans during Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour. The tour officially began July 24 at Chicago's Soldier Field. During that opening concert, Karol G spotted another relationship-themed sign in the audience, this time from a pair of newlyweds. Their message read, "Nos casamos. Queremos ir a otro show de luna de miel," which translates to, "We got married. We want to go to another show for our honeymoon." Karol G didn't simply congratulate them. After asking where they wanted to go, the singer offered to send the couple to Paris to attend another Tropitour concert. "Nos vamos de luna de miel para París y a ver el show de Karol G," she told them, meaning they were going to Paris for their honeymoon and to see her show. The Los Angeles concerts have produced their own headline-making moments. The first SoFi Stadium show on Aug. 14 launched a three-night run, while the second featured a surprise appearance from Bruno Mars for the live debut of their collaboration "Still." © ¡HOLA! title: Jungle justice: Lawyer, group commend I-G’s directive, say practice invites anarchy - Realnews Magazine
content: A security advocacy group, the Security Situation Room (SSR), has backed the Inspector-General of Police (I-G), Mr Olatunji Disu’s directive to treat jungle justice as homicide. The group described mob action as an invitation to anarchy, saying perpetrators of extra-judicial killings must be held accountable for their actions. The President of SSR, Mr Douglas Ogbankwa, told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in an interview that the directive was timely, considering the spate of mob attacks and extra-judicial killings in the country. “Of course, this directive is timely. Allowing people to resort to strong-arm tactics in solving criminal activities is an invitation to anarchy. “It is like taking the country to the Hobbesian state of nature, where life was nasty, brutish and short,” he said. Ogbankwa said the existence of government could be traced to the social contract theory, under which citizens surrendered certain liberties to enable constituted authorities to govern and protect them. He said allowing individuals to take the law into their hands would undermine the purpose of government and the rule of law. “The reason we have a government is traceable to the social contract theory, where the people agree to have people who will govern, protect them and take care of their welfare. “So, if individuals are allowed to have the liberty of taking the law into their hands, then that is simply taking us to the Stone Age without laws,” he said. The convener noted that every society was governed by laws, adding that the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (as amended) provided lawful avenues for resolving grievances. He said the Police Act 2020 empowered the police to detect and investigate crimes and arrest those suspected of committing offences within their jurisdiction. Ogbankwa consequently called for strict adherence to the I-G’s directive, adding that individuals must learn to be personally accountable for their actions or inactions. NAN reports that Disu directed Commissioners of Police across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) to treat cases of jungle justice as homicide. Disu gave the directive on Wednesday while speaking on a live television programme on African Independent Television (AIT). The police boss condemned the growing incidence of mob attacks and extra-judicial killings across the country, describing jungle justice as murder and a violation of victims’ fundamental rights. He consequently directed the arrest and prosecution of perpetrators of jungle justice. NAN reports that Disu noted that Sections 33, 34 and 36 of the 1999 Constitution guarantee every Nigerian, including suspects, the rights to life, dignity and a fair hearing. He added that no individual or group had the authority to determine the guilt of a suspect, as the law presumes every person innocent until proven guilty by a competent court. Also speaking with NAN, a Lagos-based lawyer, Mr Ademola Owolabi of Adetokunbo Ademola Chambers, Apapa, backed the directive, saying it was legally justified. Owolabi said the law was certain but not static, adding that it was a dynamic organ that must adapt to changes in society. According to him, homicide presupposes mens rea (guilty mind) and actus reus (guilty act), noting that jungle justice might not easily fit the premeditated essence of murder. He, however, said the theory of law was that a person intended the natural consequences of his actions. “If a mob chased an alleged thief, tied tyres around his neck and set him on fire, resulting in his death, they intended to kill him. “Similarly, where planks were used to beat an alleged thief and death occurred, it is obvious that the intention was to kill,” he said. Owolabi, therefore, said the I-G was right in directing the police to treat cases of jungle justice as homicide. He, however, urged the police to embrace forensic investigation to strengthen the prosecution of such cases. According to him, cases should not be charged to court solely on the basis of confessional statements, particularly where such statements appeared to have been obtained through coercion. He said where there was evidence that a mob caught an alleged criminal but refused to hand him over to the police, members of the mob could be charged with homicide. title: Biz Buzz: St. G’s Bodega moving into old hardware store in St. Cloud's East End - St. Cloud Live

ST. CLOUD — A new bodega store, St. G’s Bodega, is scheduled to open in early September on the site of an old hardware store in St. Cloud’s East End. It’ll have staple grocery items with a “New York bodega style,” St. G’s Bodega co-owner Maddie Waseka said. That means sodas, cereals, chips, cigarettes and more will all be for sale. “We wanted to add something that was a little bit higher-end than your standard grocery in looks and offered the everyday staples that people need on that side of town,” Waseka said. The location is 415 E St. Germain St., originally the old Sentinel Hardware building before it was purchased by Marla Waseka, Maddie’s mother, in 2022.       St. Cloud’s East End,
    
       or areas centered around East St. Germain Street and the Lincoln Avenue corridors, east of the Mississippi River. The long-closed hardware store now houses

The organization’s 1,200 volunteers have worked alongside more than 160 partner nonprofits, government agencies and healthcare groups. “We’re thrilled to be able to continue serving our communities,” RSVP Director Jennifer Wucherer said in a statement. “We are passionate about working with older adults — not only to help meet community needs, but also to honor and value the experience, knowledge and impact that older adults bring. The training initiative is expected to deliver measurable outcomes for both employees and the regional economy. This partnership reflects a shared commitment to building a resilient, inclusive and future-ready workforce across Central Minnesota, according to participants. title: Locality Pay: Why A GS-13 In San Francisco Earns About $30,000 More Than "Rest Of U.S." - FedSmith.com
content: 2026 federal locality pay supplements range from 17.06% to 46.34%. See how it affects GS-13 salaries, high-3 averages, and annuities across top and bottom areas. Calculating federal pay (Photo by Ian Smith/FedSmith; edited with AI) Federal employees under the General Schedule receive a base salary plus a locality payment that varies by geographic area. The 2026 rates range from 17.06% in the Rest of U.S. locality pay area to 46.34% in the San Jose-San Francisco-Oakland, CA, locality pay area. The federal locality pay system adjusts General Schedule salaries to reflect differences in non-federal pay levels across geographic regions. Authorized by the Federal Employees Pay Comparability Act of 1990, the system took effect in January 1994. Its purpose is to reduce pay disparities between federal and non-federal workers performing similar work in the same labor market. Locality payments are calculated as a percentage of base pay and applied according to the employee’s official worksite. The Office of Personnel Management publishes annual tables that incorporate both the across-the-board base pay increase and the locality adjustment for each designated area. For 2026, locality pay percentages remain at the prior year’s levels, while base pay received a 1.0% across-the-board increase. A locality pay area is a geographic region where federal employees receive an additional percentage adjustment. The President’s Pay Agent defines these areas after receiving recommendations from the Federal Salary Council. The Bureau of Labor Statistics supplies the underlying data by comparing General Schedule pay with non-federal compensation at comparable work levels. The cost of living is not a direct factor in the calculations. Pay disparity between federal and non-federal salaries is the primary driver. As of 2026, there are still 58 locality pay areas, including separate areas for Alaska and Hawaii and the residual Rest of U.S. category. These percentage differences compound over time. Prior FedSmith reporting has shown how cumulative annual differences of even 2–3 percentage points can produce salary gaps exceeding $20,000 at mid-level grades within a five-to-seven-year span. The five-year cumulative column assumes the 2026 rates remain constant for illustration. Actual future rates will vary with annual adjustments, but the table demonstrates the scale of the ongoing differential. An employee in the San Jose-San Francisco-Oakland area receives nearly $30,000 more per year than a counterpart in the Rest of U.S. area at the identical grade and step. Over five years, that gap exceeds $149,000 before taxes or benefits. Because locality pay is added to base pay, employees in high-rate areas receive higher total compensation for the same grade and step. The system therefore produces clear winners and losers in absolute salary terms. Employees stationed in the San Francisco Bay Area or New York metropolitan region benefit from the largest adjustments. Those in the Rest of U.S. category, which still covers a sizable share of the workforce, receive the smallest supplements. The expansion of locality pay areas has narrowed the Rest of U.S. share over the past decade. New areas created in recent years moved thousands of employees out of the residual category and into higher-rate tables. Once an area is designated, subsequent annual adjustments continue to reflect local pay disparities measured by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Locality pay counts as basic pay for several major benefits. According to Office of Personnel Management guidance on administering locality rates, the locality-adjusted rate is used to compute retirement deductions and benefits, life insurance premiums and benefits, premium pay, severance pay, and lump-sum payments for annual leave. This treatment means that employees in higher-locality areas contribute more to the Federal Employees Retirement System and the Civil Service Retirement System due to their higher salaries. They also receive correspondingly higher life insurance coverage under the Federal Employees’ Group Life Insurance program when coverage is tied to annual basic pay. The high-3 average salary used to calculate Federal Employees Retirement System and Civil Service Retirement System annuities includes locality pay. An employee’s three highest consecutive years of basic pay, including the applicable locality percentages, form the base for the annuity formula. Because locality rates differ by location, two employees with identical grades, steps, and years of service can retire with different monthly annuities solely because of the locality rates applied during their high-3 period. Using the 2026 GS-13, Step 5 figures, the average high-3 difference between the top-10 and bottom-10 locality areas is nearly $18,000. Under the standard Federal Employees Retirement System formula—1% of high-3 multiplied by years of service (or 1.1% for employees retiring at age 62 or later with 20 or more years)—that salary gap produces a permanent difference in the annual annuity, measured in thousands of dollars. The high-3 period is not required to be the final three years of service. If an employee worked earlier in a higher-locality area, those earlier years may form the high-3 if they produce a larger average. Conversely, transferring to a lower-locality area in the final years of a career can lock in a lower high-3 if the recent lower rates become the highest consecutive three-year average. Once the annuity is computed, the benefit is fixed and is not reduced if the retiree later moves to a lower-cost area. This means that locality pay flows directly into the high-3 average salary used to compute CSRS and FERS basic annuities. High-3 is the average of an employee’s highest three consecutive years of basic pay. For most GS employees, locality-adjusted basic pay is included. A career spent primarily in a high-percentage locality, or a late-career move into one, raises the final three years and produces a higher annuity for life. The reverse—moving to a lower-percentage area near retirement—can lower the high-3 if those years end up being the highest three. The location where an employee lives after retirement does not affect the already-computed annuity. Some employees, therefore, work in high-locality areas to maximize the high-3, then relocate to lower-cost areas. TSP contributions are also based on the higher basic pay, so higher locality pay can support larger retirement savings, though individual contribution rates and investment performance remain the primary drivers. The locality pay system continues to evolve through Federal Salary Council recommendations and presidential decisions on annual adjustments. For 2026, the published rates and area definitions remain the operative figures for salary determination, benefit calculations, and retirement planning. President Trump is expected to issue an Alternative Pay Plan for the 2027 pay rates before September 1. Presidents typically issue these plans late in the month. Expectations for a 2027 civilian pay raise remain low. A few months ago, the administration released its FY 2027 budget proposal. It had no mention of a raise for federal civilian employees. The Office of Management and Budget later confirmed that the proposal effectively calls for no pay increase. By contrast, the budget does include a military pay raise, described as follows: Pay Raise for the Troops. The Administration recognizes the importance of America’s warfighters and their families, so the Budget funds a military pay raise of seven percent for all DoD (Department of War) military personnel ranked E-5 and below, six percent for E-6 to O-3, and five percent for O-4 and above. This enduring investment, far above the standard annual military pay raise, builds on the President’s recruiting and retention success, by doubling down on the Administration’s goal to restore America’s fighting force. This mirrors last year’s process. The FY 2026 budget proposal also omitted a civilian raise. The subsequent alternative pay plan provided a 1% across-the-board increase and no locality pay increase for most employees (with higher adjustments for certain law enforcement personnel). A similar alternative pay plan is possible this year. If any civilian raise materializes—whether across-the-board only or with a locality component—it is likely to be relatively small. As of mid-August 2026, Congress has not advanced language that would override a low or zero civilian increase. Federal employees in locality pay areas will continue to earn more than those in the Rest of U.S. schedule. The highest-paying locality areas are expected to remain at or near the top of the rankings. © 2026 Ralph R. Smith. All rights reserved. Wi-Fi Spec: BE18000Number of Antennas/Removable: 8/NoPorts: Input WAN – One 2.5 Gbps WAN; Seven 2.5Gbps LAN; USB 3.0 (Gen 1)Processor/Memory/Storage: Quad-core 2.0 GHz/2GB/256 MBWi-Fi chips: Broadcom BCM6766802.11be performance: 2.354 Gbps (at 15 feet)Range: 130 feetSize: 8.9 x 8.9 x 3.5 inchesEstimated Annual Electricity Cost: $27.13 At $400, Asus resets the bar for high performance gaming routers with its ROG Strix GS-BE18000. Its appearance may be plain Jane but the GS-BE18000 could be the year’s stealth gaming router with everything needed to battle the world on your terms. From top triband Wi-Fi 7 speeds to access to gaming accelerators to 8 networking ports, it separates itself from the rest of the best Wi-Fi 7 routers. Among the first to implement Automated Frequency Coordination (AFC), it features better speed, range and reliability than competitors. It doesn’t matter if you’re a Leaguer or Minecrafter, the ROG Strix GS-BE18000 is not only small and modestly priced but has the power to blast your gaming into another dimension. Read on to see if this is the best gaming router for your battlestation. With a list price of $450, it pays to shop around for the Asus ROG Strix GS-BE18000. It’s available at Best Buy for $400, making it an excellent bargain that can outperform and outplay routers selling for hundreds more. The slightly less powerful ROG Strix GS-BE12000 also sells for $350 at Walmart. Considering all the Asus ROG Strix GS-BE18000 can do, it is amazing that it is roughly the size of a shoe box at 8.9 x 8.9 x 3.4 inches. That’s less than one quarter the size of the company’s ROG Rapture GT-BE19000AI router with its eight antennas pointing every which way. Available only in black, the ROG Strix GS-BE18000 is anything but intimidating looking. In fact, its boxy appearance is high on the Meh scale and not what I expect when it comes to a fire-breathing gaming router. Still, it’s what’s inside that counts, starting with Broadcom’s BCM6766 Wi-Fi chip, a 2.0GHz quad-core processor, 2GB of RAM and 256MB of flash storage for the device’s firmware and settings. It lacks the dedicated AI hardware that graces the GT-BE19000AI router, though this 8-stream router takes advantage of 320MHz data channels, Multi-Link Operations (MLO) and 4K Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM). Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips. It’s among the first to tap into the higher transmission power available through 6GHz Automated Frequency Coordination (AFC) for faster data speeds, longer range and higher reliability. Using AFC is rare today and only works in the U.S., Canada, U.K. and Saudi Arabia. Look for the circle to widen over time. Able to work on all three Wi-Fi 7 bands, the GS-BE18000 features 4X4 streaming for the 5.0 and 6.0GHz transmissions, while the 2.4 GHz band is limited to 2X2 action. It adds up to a throughput rating of 18.0 Gbps. All the router’s networking ports can handle 2.5 Gbps wired traffic. In addition to the input WAN port, the GS-BE18000 has a generous seven downstream LAN connections. There’s also a Gen 1 USB 3.0 port for running a print server, making the contents of a data drive active across the LAN or using a mobile phone as a backup Internet feed when your broadband goes south. In the back are buttons for using the Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) for quickie client connections and turning the router on or off. It can run as a Wi-Fi router, wired access point or a wireless node in an AiMesh network. Its excellent Quality of Service protocol is integrated into the gaming features for top access to data. It may lack the GT-BE19000AI’s window to see its components inside, but the GS-BE18000 has the router’s key specs embossed on a raised strip. There’s no info screen although its LEDs light up the ROG logo in any of seven visual effects and choice of color. Its pattern doesn’t change when the router goes offline but the stack of four LEDs below has indicators for WAN, WiFi, LAN and Power. Passively cooled, the GS-BE18000 has innovative nanocarbon-coated aluminum heat sink fins to transfer heat away from the router’s sensitive electronic components. It draws room air in from the bottom and expels hot air from the sides and top and peaked at 103.7 degrees Fahrenheit. The router is secured by Asus’s AIProtection security software that includes ad blocking, web filtering and malware protection. It stands out from the crowd (including Netgear’s Armor) by being a no-fee service that includes continual updates to thwart the nastiest attacks. The three-year warranty and life of product support blow away the competition. The router’s support pages have the expected set up tips and firmware downloads, but the 32-page manual seems rudimentary if you print it. Meant for online use, it has dozens of internal links for set up and operation tips. Based on extensive testing using Keysight’s IxChariot networking benchmark and my HP Envy X360 notebook, the ROG Strix GS-BE18000 zoomed past competitors, making it an excellent online companion. With the software set to simulate 10 data hungry users and the router next to the test machine, the GS-BE18000 moved 2.238 Gbps of data over Wi-Fi and 4.465 Gbps over 15 feet of Cat 7 cabling. This puts it in the upper echelon of high-performance routers. At the real-world distance of 15 feet, the GS-BE18000 delivered 2.354 Gbps of live data, putting it between the TP-Link Archer BE770 at 2.181 Gbps and the Asus ROG Rapture GS-BE19000AI at 2.580 Gbps. It’s more than enough for those with multi-gig data plans. With the router and test system 50 feet apart, the GS-BE18000 dominated at 1.354 Gbps, ahead of the Archer BE770’s 1.239 Gbps and one-third more throughput than the GT-BE19000AI’s 1.006 Gbps. At 75 feet, its 900.8 Mbps topped the Archer BE770 (at 772.1 Mbps) and the GT-BE19000AI (528.3 Mbps). Its 40.9 Mbps reading at 90 feet was more mundane and beaten by the Archer BE770’s 70.9 Mbps and the GT-BE19000AI’s 49.1 Mbps. Its 100-foot range should satisfy those living in mid-sized homes but is off the Archer BE770’s 130 feet. Finally, the GS-BE18000 moved upwards of 1.309 Gbps to a room 25 feet away. That’s among the best and shows the device’s ability to efficiently fill a home with data. During my two weeks with the GS-BE18000, it showed itself to be reliable and fast, although it left a couple dead zones in the attic and basement. While in use, it consumed 17.7 watts of electricity for an annual estimated power bill of about $27.13 if it runs all day and night and you pay the national average of 17.5 cents per kilowatt hour of electricity. By contrast, the Archer BE770 was a power hog at about $36 a year. It took 5 minutes to set the ROG Strix GS-BE18000 up using the Asus Router app. After I plugged everything in, I needed to pick a picture of the router, although nothing in the interface matched. The closest was “WiFi routers” and the process was automatic. I added names and passwords. It can all be done through the router’s online interface at asusrouter.com Like other Asus routers, the app is where to customize its settings. The home screen shows the current LED lighting effect as well as links to the current speed, the Internet connection status and the gaming goodies. Below are tabs for Devices (number of online devices without tapping), Insight (for firmware updates) and Family (for Web filtering by age group). The Settings tab has everything from Diagnostics and Gaming to QOS and Wi-Fi details. The router’s browser interface’s main page is incredibly dense. In addition to the current traffic and IP addresses, there’s the LED lighting effects too. The ROG Strix GS-Be18000’s Game Mode not only shows the current latency specs and deviation, but packet loses along the way. It can be set as the top data dog in the house, making your gaming the priority. Diehard gamers will love the global Ping map. The game accelerators can speed up the action for seven online games. They range from World of Tanks to Diablo 3. If the economy’s overpriced and everything has got you down, the Asus ROG Strix GS-BE18000 is a genuine bargain that can move data as fast or faster than devices selling for much more. In addition to a generous eight 2.5 Gbps wired networking ports, the GS-BE18000 uses the latest Wi-Fi tricks to deliver more than 2 Gbps available over Wi-Fi and includes an excellent AFC implementation for increasing the power and reach of the 6GHz band At $400, it’s money well spent on filling a home with high-speed gaming data. I just wish it would menace my gaming friends more. Brian Nadel is a freelance writer and editor who specializes in technology reporting and reviewing. He works out of the suburban New York City area and has covered topics from nuclear power plants and Wi-Fi routers to cars and tablets. title: BMW F 650 GS Spied Testing: India Launch Expected In 2028 - ZigWheels.com
content: BMW Motorrad is preparing to enter a new battleground in the adventure bike segment. An early prototype has been spotted testing, and it is of a new middleweight GS. With this bike, the German bikemaker directly plans to go against the highly successful Yamaha Ténéré 700. This new model will slot into the big gap in BMW’s lineup between the new F 450 GS and the larger F 900 GS, using a new iteration of its parallel-twin engine. The upcoming motorcycle aims to attract a new set of customers by blending capabilities from across the existing GS family. While the final name is yet to be confirmed, the strategy which BMW is going for is clear. It plans to target the popular middleweight adventure category, a space where BMW currently lacks a contender. The upcoming bike’s design and hardware suggest a motorcycle that is more substantial and off-road focused than the F 450 GS but likely more accessible and lighter than the F 900 GS. Early photos of the test mule show a blend of all the familiar GS components which we have seen on various bikes. From the way the rear shock is mounted to the swingarm design, they appear similar to the smaller F 450 GS. However, the bike's overall presence is considerably more mature, rolling on proper off-road-spec tubless spoke wheels: a 21-inch front and an 17-inch rear. While the steel bridge frame and braking system seem to be derived from its bigger sibling, the F 900 GS. Although the fairing seems temporary, the headlight design looks derived from and inspired by the flagship R 1300 GS, though the characteristic GS ‘beak’ is currently missing. We expect the heart of this new BMW bike to be a completely new unit. It will not be based on the 450 GS, the F 900 GS or the Norton Atlas. That said, we do expect the engine capacity to be somewhere around the 650cc mark and the power output too to be around 70-80 PS. This will allow the bike to go squarely against the Yamaha Ténéré 700, the Honda XL750 Transalp and the Suzuki V-Strom 800 DE. The prototype seen appears to be in an early stages of development, with significant work still needed before it's ready for production. A global launch is therefore not expected to take place before 2028. While there is no official announcement about its India launch, we expect the bike to make its way to our shores soon after it's available internationally. As for the price, it will sit right in between the F 450 GS and the F 900 GS, at around Rs 12 lakh (ex-showroom). Thanks for reporting this. title: New BMW Middleweight Adventure Bike Spied Testing; Could Be the F 650 GS - bikewale.com
content: Get Notifications on Latest UpdatesBMW Motorrad appears to be working on a new middleweight adventure motorcycle that could sit between the F 450 GS and F 800 GS in its global line-up. A test prototype of the motorcycle has been spotted, revealing several similarities to BMW’s existing GS models, although the production-specification details are still unclear. The motorcycle appears to use a parallel-twin engine and shares some technical elements with the recently introduced F 450 GS. However, its chassis and braking hardware are closer to BMW’s larger adventure motorcycles like the F 800 GS and the F 900 GS. The prototype rides on a 21-inch front and 18-inch rear wheel combination, suggesting it could offer stronger off-road capability. One of the biggest questions surrounding the motorcycle is its engine. Although it isn’t confirmed yet, BMW could use a heavily reworked version of the parallel-twin platform that powers the F 450 GS. BMW’s partner TVS uses a heavily revised version of this engine in the Norton Atlas, where the 585cc produces 70bhp. However, it remains unclear whether BMW’s motorcycle will use the same displacement or a different configuration. We expect a power output in the ballpark of 65bhp to 70bhp. That said, the BMW adventure bike will be a more off-road-focused model compared to the Norton Atlas. The prototype features a steel bridge frame that appears closer in design to the F 900 GS than the F 450 GS. Its braking system also appears to have been derived from the larger GS, while the 21-inch front and 18-inch rear wheels point towards genuine off-road capability. The motorcycle appears to be in the early development stage, with unfinished bodywork, especially around the fairing. That said, the X-style headlight seems to have taken inspiration from the BMW R 1300 GS, although the familiar GS beak is absent from the prototype. BMW has not revealed the motorcycle’s name. An F 600 GS nomenclature would fit if the engine displacement is around 600cc. However, BMW could also revive the F 650 GS name, which was previously used for its middleweight adventure motorcycles. Given the unfinished bodywork, the motorcycle seems to be at the nascent stage of development. As a result, a production version is likely to be launched sometime in 2028. When launched, this BMW adventure bike could rival the Yamaha Ténéré 700 and the upcoming KTM 690 Rally.

title: GS Global opens Houston office to target US energy projects - The Korea Herald
content:
Business GS Global opens Houston office to target US energy projects GS Global said Monday it has opened an office in Houston to expand its presence in the US energy and infrastructure markets. Located in Houston’s Uptown district, the office will target growing demand for project-based steel generated by increased investment in energy, power and infrastructure. GS Global previously managed most of its US business through its Los Angeles office. The company said the new base would help it respond more quickly to shifting market conditions, including stronger protectionism and global supply chain restructuring. The Houston office will seek and support steel orders for major projects while expanding the company’s role in the US energy value chain. It will also explore opportunities in chemicals, energy and shipbuilding equipment. GS Global plans to work with Korean steelmakers operating in the Houston area, including Hyundai Steel and Dongkuk Steel, while cultivating local engineering, procurement and construction companies and steel fabricators as customers. During the second half, the company will focus on building a local network and strengthening its project pipeline. From 2027, it plans to expand order support and pursue new businesses, positioning Houston as a key development hub for the southern US. “The Houston office is a strategic investment aimed at expanding our customer base and strengthening our sales competitiveness in the US,” a GS Global official said. “We will pursue opportunities beyond project-based steel to establish a sustainable foundation for growth in North America.” Trump says North Korea's Kim has responded to his overtures A day after he ordered the United States to scale back military exercises with South Korea, US President Donald Trump said on Monday that North Korean leader Kim Jong-un had responded to his outreach. title: Rucsu GS Ammar organises 'July Ziyafat' with cow named 'Baksal', drawing students' backlash over funding - tbsnews.net
content: A 'July feast' featuring a cow named 'Baksal' was organised at Rajshahi University (RU) today (15 August), with Rajshahi University Central Students' Union (Rucsu) General Secretary Salauddin Ammar taking a leading role in the event. The feast was held at the university's Central Mosque premises at around 2pm, in which, according to the organisers, some 750 students participated. Students were invited to register through a Google Form. The use of the Rucsu's imagery in the banner for the event drew mixed reactions from the students on social media, with some questioning whether union funds were used to organise the feast. In a Facebook post, RU student Kaushik Das Kangkan said, "Salauddin Ammar is sacrificing a cow in Rucsu's name using the students' money. Who gave him the right to waste their money like this?" However, Rucsu's Debate and Literature Secretary Imran Laskar said that he was unaware whether the cow was being sacrificed on behalf of the student union and denied any involvement in the event. "I want to make it clear that I have no involvement with this event. Those organising it under the Rucsu's banner have not yet given a clear statement about it," he added, urging those involved to clarify the matter to the students. Mehedi Maruf, president of the university unit of Chhatra Odhikar Parishad, questioned the source of funding for the event. "If this is not Rucsu's money, then whose money is it?" he said, alleging that students' money could be being used for political purposes. Several students also criticised the initiative on social media, raising concerns over the quality of food in residential halls, internet services and accommodation facilities. In a video message posted on Facebook last night, Ammar announced the feast and said the cow had been named 'Baksal'. He said the animal would be sacrificed as part of the celebrations, describing the event as a "July Ziyafat" ("July Feast"). Speaking to reporters at the feast, Ammar said today marked what he described as the "historic fall of Baksal" and the second anniversary of the July Uprising, which was why the cow had been given such a name. He said Rucsu had initially promoted the event, but not all union members agreed with it. Later, he alleged, "the cow was gifted by an individual and the union was not involved in the matter". This afternoon, students were seen gathering in small groups near the Central Mosque. Food packets were being prepared inside the Rucsu building, while tarpaulins were being laid on the grass outside the premises for students to sit and eat. title: The Buick Muscle Car That Made More Torque Than An LS6 Chevelle - HotCars
content: There’s one Buick muscle car that’s being unfairly forgotten despite being a stout sleeper option that packs a luxury punch. The golden-era Buick actually has more torque than a Chevelle rocking LS6 power. But you would never know that based on auction values alone. The Chevelle LS6 is busy hogging the spotlight, while an unsuspecting Buick could embarrass it at stoplights. But unfortunately, when the "Dad" label is applied to tire-shredding monsters, they often get overlooked in favor of flashier options. In 1964,     General Motors imposed a corporate mandate that prevented midsize cars from using V8 engines with over 400 cubic inches, in order to cut down on internal power battles with the Corvette and to comply with increasing safety and regulatory concerns. Muscle cars were pretty dangerous and difficult to control as their popularity began to explode. But divisions like Pontiac and Chevrolet used factory loopholes and specific central office production orders, like COPO systems, to skirt around the rules. This enabled them to keep up with racing rivals from Ford and Chrysler with the ability to stuff massive blocks into smaller and lighter cars. The reluctance of divisions to give up massive amounts of V8 power by getting around the rules, as Ford and Chrysler continued to build them, proved that customer demand was there. The desire for bigger engines was taking performance-oriented buyers away from General Motors showrooms. So, in 1970, the ban was finally lifted, and suddenly Buick needed more power to remain competitive. Back in the 1960s, Buick had a reputation for being a brand that made luxury cruisers for older folks. It sort of still has that reputation today despite trying to erase it while targeting more youthful buyers with high-performance excitement. This is why the 1970 Buick GS 455 Stage 1 was built to dominate drag strips. This Buick has a 455 cubic-inch (7.5-liter) big-block V8 under the hood that delivers 360 horsepower and 510 lb-ft of torque. But these figures are widely believed to be underrated, as dyno tests reveal the actual power output to be closer to 400–415 hp and 515 lb-ft of torque. It may have been intentionally underrated to avoid insurance surcharges and corporate policies. The Stage 1 package adds a larger 2.12-inch intake and a 1.77-inch exhaust, stiffer valve springs, a more aggressive high-lift camshaft, a rejetted high-flow Rochester Quadrajet carburetor, functional hood scoops, and a Turbo Hydra-matic transmission with governor tweaks for higher shift points. It can accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in roughly 6.4 seconds and complete a quarter mile in about 13.3 seconds with a top speed of 135 mph. Meanwhile, the 1970 Chevy Chevelle 454 LS6 had a 454 cubic-inch (7.4-liter) V8 engine with 450 hp and 500 lb-ft of torque. This car reaches 60 mph in roughly 5.4 seconds with a 13.12-second quarter-mile time at 108 mph and a top speed of 140 mph. Despite having enough power to give the     Chevelle SS LS6 454 a run for its money, the Buick GS 455 Stage 1 failed to win over buyers. It was seen as underpowered in comparison, due to a factory rating of only 360 hp compared to 450 hp, despite having more torque, making it the ultimate sleeper model. Buick was still seen as a luxury brand for older, more mature buyers. Meanwhile, the Chevelle SS was heavily marketed toward younger buyers looking for high-powered thrills. It was seen as a more affordable icon with a massive pop culture presence. Plus, it was often promoted with brighter paint schemes and bold racing stripes. Both cars actually offered luxury comfort with available features such as bucket seats, deluxe steering wheels, padded dashboards, and optional rounded gauges. However, Buick took things a step further with upgraded upholstery, deep-twist carpeting, GS badging, wood-grain accents, molded door panels, armrests, and rear-seat speakers. Despite being more luxurious, the Buick GS 455 was the more affordable option with an original MSRP of $3,283. Adding the $199 Stage 1 Performance package increased the price to $3,482. After checking all the boxes for the 1970 Chevy Chevelle SS LS6 454, the starting price hovered between $3,500 and $3,800. But the base model started at $2,809. You can get big block V8 power for a much lower price in the Buick GS Stage 1 instead of the Chevelle SS LS6, even though the Buick models are harder to find. Only about 2,697 Buick GS 455 Stage 1 models were built in 1970, including 664 cars with the manual transmission and 232 convertibles. In comparison, about 4,475 1970 Chevy Chevelle SS LS6 454 models were made. Roughly 500 of the engines may have been placed in the El Camino instead. Chevrolet didn't break down individual production figures for hardtop and convertible models, and historians believe under 400 convertibles exist. Buick GS 455 Stage 1 models typically go for $45,000 to $65,000 if found in good, driving condition. These models found in excellent condition generally fetch between $75,000 and $110,000 at auction. Buick GS 455 cars in pristine quality can sell for between $130,000 and over $200,000. Convertibles and models with the manual transmission command the highest premiums. 1970 Chevy Chevelle SS 454 LS6 models in driving condition are snatched up for between $95,000 and $120,000. Examples in excellent condition cross the auction block for around $150,000 to $185,000. But models found in pristine or show-ready condition go for between $100,000 and over $250,000. title: Hear Becky G's New Album 'Baraja Bendita' - antiMusic
content: (align) Becky G releases her fifth studio album, BARAJA BENDITA, an 17-track body of work that stands as the most complete artistic statement of her career via RCA Records. The album's focus track, "CHULA," is an ode to a word that carries many meanings across Latin culture, centering on its use as a term of endearment while embracing its duality as both an expression of affection and a celebration of confidence, beauty, and "baddie" energy. Written as a singular body of work without guest features, BARAJA BENDITA finds Becky stepping fully into her own authorship, creating an album defined not by reinvention, but by wholeness. Her decision to build an entire album by herself was executed out of creative necessity, the 17 tracks showcase the world she built herself, on her own terms and with her own story-telling of what it means to be fully known. Rather than introducing a new version of herself, the project presents every version at once-allowing vulnerability and confidence, instinct and intention, to exist side by side. Grounded in the symbolism and strategy of a deck of cards, BARAJA BENDITA explores the idea of agency over chance. It's not about the hand you're dealt, but about becoming the one who deals it. Each song represents a different move, perspective, and emotional state, shifting in meaning as it unfolds within the larger narrative. Together, the songs create a world where control and unpredictability coexist, reflecting the complexity of identity while embracing every side of Becky. Throughout the project, she introduces BB as a creative signature that bridges Becky G, Rebbeca, and BARAJA BENDITA: a symbol of duality, ownership, and the freedom to exist fully without contradiction. "BARAJA BENDITA is about trusting myself enough to stop choosing between different parts of who I am," says Becky G. "For so long, people wanted to define me by one thing: one language, one sound, one version of myself. This album isn't about becoming someone new. It's about fully owning every part of who I've always been." The "2AM" VEVO Official Live Performance offers a glimpse into the visual world of Becky G's BARAJA BENDITA, bringing the song's intimate energy to life through a dreamlike setting filled with rich textures, warm tones, and layered details. This video marks the first installment of an exclusive series of performance videos rolling out over the coming weeks. Working alongside an accomplished roster of collaborators, Becky crafted an expansive sonic landscape where every track stands on its own while contributing to a cohesive emotional journey. Moving seamlessly between pop, Latin, electronic, alternative, and urban influences, BARAJA BENDITA allows every sound to serve the story rather than define it. The firm's operational attention remains fixed on these channels, which together drive its business and which contributed to the standout season. Sustaining strength across trading and dealmaking requires the reliable execution of these activities as market conditions evolve. Managing exposure also forms a central part of the operational picture, since a capital-markets firm takes on exposure through its trading and underwriting activities. Balancing the pursuit of activity with prudent management of that exposure is an ongoing discipline, and it sits alongside the firm's efforts to serve its clients and capture the revival in dealmaking. The blend of activity and disciplined exposure management defines much of how the firm operates day to day. Despite the standout season, the capital-markets industry faces genuine challenges. The cyclical nature of dealmaking means that a revival can give way to a quieter stretch as conditions shift, introducing variability into the business. Trading revenue depends on active markets, and a calmer environment can dampen it. Competition among Wall Street banks for advisory and underwriting work is intense, with firms vying for the same transactions and listings. Regulatory attention to capital-markets activity adds complexity, requiring firms to devote resources to compliance and capital management. Goldman Sachs must navigate these challenges while continuing to capture activity across its engines. The record trading revenue and the dealmaking rebound demonstrated its ability to do so under current conditions, but the challenges remain constant companions in the capital-markets business. Sustaining strength across trading and dealmaking requires ongoing effort across every part of the enterprise, from client relationships to exposure management to the execution that turns a reviving cycle into results. The competitive landscape for Goldman Sachs spans several categories of rivals. It competes with other large Wall Street banks for advisory and underwriting mandates, for trading flows, and for the relationships with corporations and institutions that generate that work. It competes with asset managers for the money it oversees on behalf of clients. And it increasingly contends with a range of firms that have entered pieces of the capital-markets chain. Within this landscape, Goldman Sachs differentiates itself through its prominence, its breadth across trading and dealmaking, and its deep client relationships. The record trading revenue and the rebound in dealmaking positioned the firm favorably within this competitive field, indicating that it captured a robust share of activity as the capital-markets cycle turned. The season served as evidence that the firm's prominent standing and its breadth across businesses continued to resonate with the corporations and institutions it serves, a meaningful signal in a segment where competition for transactions and trading flows is relentless. The relevance of this earnings season's results extends beyond Goldman Sachs itself. Because the firm sits at the center of trading and dealmaking, its results offer a read on the health of capital-markets activity across the economy. The record trading revenue and the rebound in dealmaking and public listings signaled a revival in that activity, feeding into the wider conversation about the direction of markets and corporate confidence. This makes the results a data point that observers of the broader group of financial stocks watch closely as an indicator of capital-markets vitality. For those following the capital-markets corner of the market, the season illustrated how a single firm's results can carry meaning well beyond one company. Goldman Sachs, through the strength of its trading and the revival of its deal pipeline, offered a snapshot of reawakening activity across the financial landscape. The pairing of record trading revenue with a dealmaking rebound underscored the firm's central role on Wall Street and its usefulness as a barometer of capital-markets conditions. title: Karol G's Latin American fantasia lands elegantly at SoFi Stadium - Yahoo News Canada
content: On Friday night at the SoFi Stadium, there was nothing random about the songs that played just before Karol G took the stage for the first of three evenings at the venue. We can safely assume that the Colombian superstar selected the cuts herself — the perfect tropicoqueta mix to set up the mood. First, a shadowy "Bésame Mucho"; Elvis Crespo's merengue smash "Suavemente"; the Afro-Cuban nugget "El Manisero"; and two life-affirming hits by the Queen of Salsa herself, Celia Cruz: "La Vida Es Un Carnaval" and "La Negra Tiene Tumbao." These carefully curated gems share a common element: They managed to transcend the stylistic contours of their respective genres and become something bigger — the kind of irresistible, it-takes-a-village anthems that will lure everyone to the dance floor, even if they don't understand the lyrics. And that is exactly what Karol G — la bichota, the South American Cleopatra, the woman with the billion-dollar smile — has been doing for global pop since the release of "Tusa," her imperial duet with Nicki Minaj, back in 2019. Karol is currently the 42nd-most-streamed artist on Spotify, and her albums "Mañana Será Bonito" (2023) and "Tropicoqueta" (2025) helped reinvent the sound of contemporary Latin. She emerged from the reggaeton thunderstorm that hijacked the planet, but then guided it smoothly into a different aesthetic territory, far away from the movement's misogynistic toxicity. Her ongoing collaboration with producer Ovy On The Drums — they're the same age, 35, both from Medellín — was transformative, combining clanging, tribal beats with liquid textures and a refined, champagne-like lightness. Part of the massive "Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour," Friday's performance confirmed the singer's stature as one of the most vital and charismatic Latin artists of the 21st century. More than a conventional concert, it felt like a stark, delirious fantasia, a relentless cinematic mosaic of decadent dance numbers and hyper-popped fragmentation presented in five acts, unified by a tropical visual motif: lush vegetation; a blue lagoon where cleansing erotic rituals take place; plumes of purifying fire to expiate the aftertaste of all those failed romances. Beginning with the wicked reggaeton beat of "Latina Foreva" — an existential jam about curves and pleasure, the freedom of the flesh — Karol ignited a deafening roar of adoration from the full-capacity crowd. For a moment, I got a taste of what Beatlemania must have sounded like in the 1960s. As the cameras followed her closely, projecting every playful grimace and flirtatious wink onto the giant video screens, the complexity of her artistic persona became increasingly transparent: an indomitable woman who is deeply connected with primal joy and sensuality, but also vulnerable enough to get her heart broken on the way to the red carpet (and still embrace the experience). In the world of Karol G, what doesn't kill you makes for an international hit. Admittedly, it was the aggressive, in-your-face numbers that worked best. Karol sounds even better when surrounded by half-naked dancers — "Gatúbela" and "Ojos Ferrari" were highlights in that respect — and the choreography evoked the sweaty rapture of a full-blown Roman orgy. But she's also smart enough to alternate the futurism of neo-reggaeton (the cutting-edge territory where her work with producers like Ovy On The Drums and Tainy has given us some astonishing records) with an affectionate nod to the past glories of Afro-Caribbean lore: the 20th century cultural bubble where Colombian families listened to the "14 Cañonazos Bailables" compilations during the Christmas season. On the title track of "Tropicoqueta," she draws an imaginary line that connects her current sexual emancipation to the frisky downbeats of 1950s mambo and the early 2000s movement that jazzed up the Afro-Caribbean classics with a digital bounce. On Friday, she salsified "Provenza" and added the riff of Willie Colón's "La Murga" as an intro to "Tusa." Her visual recreation of the "Tropicoqueta" album cover onstage was one of the show's wittiest moments. At one point after the success of "Mañana Será Bonito," Karol must have realized that her newly acquired diva status gave her the chance to voice some valuable thoughts on the merits of Latin American culture. In between songs, Karol spoke with compassion about the recent earthquakes affecting Colombia and Venezuela — the latter of which is where her poised opening act, Elena Rose, also hails from — but her pan-Latino ideology seeped into the music as well. Her face was covered in tears after she performed "Ese Hombre Es Malo" backed by female mariachi players. At the end of the show, a stunning reading of "Si Antes Te Hubiera Conocido" revealed the instinctive ease with which she can navigate the sweet, syncopated phrasing of Dominican merengue. A few tracks from her recently released sixth studio album,"No Me Arrepiento De Sentir Tanto," displayed a more introspective side. On the dreamy ballad "Después de Ti," she was joined on guitar by Greg Gonzalez of Cigarettes After Sex, reenacting their performance together from April, when Karol headlined Coachella. The deafening volume at SoFi was the only aspect of the show that got in the way. The sound stage felt bludgeoned into submission throughout, as the intense distortion of bass, percussion and guitars made the instrument separation within the mix almost inaudible. That said, the overall experience transcended the sonic elements, as Karol is clearly using the Tropitour as a good reason to celebrate her extraordinary achievements with the fans (she even hugged a security guard). Somewhere in the venue, a young Latina girl must have been dazzled by this extravagant spectacle and perhaps dreamed of one day following in the footsteps of Carolina Giraldo Navarro: a gifted singer and composer, a woman intelligent enough to cherish the emotional value of dancing the night away. title: Positives on both sides of the ball highlight GS Football first scrimmage - Grice Connect
content:
The Georgia Southern football squad held its first scrimmage of preseason camp Saturday night under the lights of Allen E. Paulson. The offense scored five touchdowns and the defense recorded three turnovers as both sides saw positive results.

Quarterbacks Max Johnson, Turner Helton, Weston Bryan and Harrison Faulkner Jr. combined to throw four touchdowns and for over 350 yards while Ty Cummings contributed a touchdown on the ground. Andre Greene Jr., King Phillips, Zay Hilliard and Antavious Murphy all had a score with Greene totaling nearly 100 yards receiving.

Defensively, AJ Brown Sr. and Phillip Gladney both had an interception.

Donal Dempsey connected on all five field goals and Tripp Bryant hit 3-of-4 field goals.

The team will return to the field on Monday and will hold its final open scrimmage of the preseason next Saturday.

title: Why Did Banking Stocks GS, JPM, BAC Surge To 52-Week Highs Today? - Stocktwits
content: Shares of Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (GS), JPMorgan Chase & Co. (JPM), and Bank of America Corp. (BAC) surged to annual highs after the banks posted stellar second-quarter earnings results that beat market expectations. GS stock led the climb among banking stocks, surging more than 9% after its record Q2 results triggered a buy-in. JPM stock rose 2.5% after its results surged past Wall Street expectations, while BAC stock also soared nearly 2% to a record high. GS stock climbed to a record high of $1,143.84 on Tuesday after the company reported record Q2 results that tore past analysts’ expectations. Goldman Sachs posted quarterly revenue of $20.98 billion, significantly higher than Wall Street's $16.4 billion estimate, according to Koyfin data. The investment bank also reported earnings of $15.91 per share, ahead of the $14.40 consensus estimate, while net income reached a record $6.32 billion for the quarter. The strong results were fueled by robust performance in investment banking, equities trading, and asset management, as companies continued to tap capital markets and pursue AI-related financing and strategic deals. "There's a lot of capital out there," CEO David Solomon said in an interview with CNBC on Tuesday. "I'm not concerned about the ability for the capital to be available for things that make sense." GS stock has surged nearly 25% so far this year. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment was ‘extremely bullish’ at the time of writing. JPM stock climbed to a 52-week high of $344.73 on Tuesday, driven by strong Q2 results that boosted investor interest in the company. The bank posted revenue of $57.35 billion versus a consensus estimate of $51.3 billion, while earnings per share (EPS) came in at $7.70 per share versus an expectation of $ 5.80 per share, based on Fiscal.ai data. JPMorgan delivered its strongest trading quarter on record, with trading revenue jumping 35% year over year to $12.1 billion. CEO Jamie Dimon said every business segment achieved record results, noting that market conditions remain favorable for sustained activity. Investment banking fees climbed 30% from a year earlier to $3.3 billion, marking their highest level since 2021, while net interest income rose 10% year over year to $25.6 billion. Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs raised the price target on the bank to $418 from $411 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating on the shares after its Q2 earnings beat, as per TheFly. JPM stock has gained more than 5% so far this year as retail sentiment improved from ‘bullish’ to ‘extremely bullish’ over 24 hours. BAC stock also climbed to a record high of $61.21 on Tuesday, driven by Q2 results that demonstrated a strong investment banking pipeline amid growing AI demand. The bank reported revenue of $31.6 billion, ahead of analyst estimates of $30.7 billion. Meanwhile, earnings per share (EPS) came in at $1.21, beating expectations of $1.13 EPS. Investment banking revenue climbed 50% year-over-year, with sales and trading revenue rising 30%. A surge of more than 70% in equities trading was the standout performer, contributing to one of the bank's best quarters in recent years. "We still have very strong pipelines in investment banking. The IPOs and deals are still getting done, and very strong interest in doing transactions,” CEO Brian Moynihan told CNBC in an interview. "The AI buildout still has a lot of debt funding and other funding required, so it's a very good environment." Meanwhile, Jefferies raised the price target on Bank of America to $75 from $70 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating on the shares after a "strong quarter," as per TheFly. BAC stock has gained more than 8% so far this year as retail sentiment improved from ‘neutral’ to ‘bullish’ over 24 hours. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Oracle has a huge backlog of cloud orders, but the company is taking on more debt to build the data centers needed to complete those contracts. Dow futures were up 0.05%, S&P 500 futures climbed 0.18%, and Nasdaq-100 futures climbed 0.61% at 10:20 PM EDT. Among ETFs tracking benchmark indexes, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) and the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) were trading higher with sentiment in the ‘bullish’ territory. The S&P 500 was up 0.38%, while the Dow closed marginally higher, up 0.02%. The strongest boost for U.S. markets on Tuesday came from lower-than-expected June inflation. According to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), the Consumer Price Index (CPI) climbed 3.5% year-on-year, below market expectations. Meanwhile, core inflation came in at 2.6%, with prices declining 0.4% from the previous month, the largest monthly drop since May 2020. Lower energy costs drove the decline in headline inflation, with the energy index falling 5.7% in June. The softer inflation figures lowered expectations for a rate hike from the Federal Reserve. According to the CME's FedWatch tool, the probability of a rate hike at the July meeting fell to 15.5%, down from 41.7% a day earlier. Mohamed El-Erian, Chief Economic Advisor at Allianz, said on Tuesday that the lower inflation figures “should help temper what had become an excessively hawkish market tilt to the monetary policy outlook.” However, he warned that the softer print “won't fully resolve the debate over the forward-looking relevance of these numbers.” However, markets reacted positively to the lower inflation figures, with chipmaking stocks such as Nvidia Corp. Additionally, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh testified before Congress on Tuesday, telling lawmakers that he expects the inflationary surge that has defined the past five years to fade into history.
